alignmentDisclaimer: External standards and frameworks are alignment references only. They do not establish certification, conformance, regulatory compliance, or third-party endorsement.
principles: People remain the final authority for protected actions.
Security and privacy controls fail closed where authority is uncertain.
Consequential actions must be attributable and auditable.
Understanding Genesis and its trust status must not depend on technical expertise or payment.

maturityLabels.Verified: Current implementation plus reproducible evidence demonstrates the complete claim within its stated scope.
maturityLabels.Tested: Relevant implementation and automated validation exist, but the broader end-to-end claim is not fully verified.
maturityLabels.Implemented: The control or governance rule exists, but current automated evidence does not prove the complete public claim.
maturityLabels.Target: Required architecture or behavior is defined but not sufficiently implemented and evidenced.
maturityLabels.Not available: The capability is intentionally unavailable until its required safety and evidence gates pass.

questions.question: Who is ultimately in control: the human or Genesis?
questions.plainLanguageAnswer: For protected actions, the human is the final project authority. Genesis may analyze, recommend and prepare actions, but it may not create its own permission.
questions.currentTruth: Owner Law and the Genesis Constitution establish human sovereignty. Cryptographic L5 enforcement is still a Target.
questions.peopleImpact: A person must not lose authority merely because an AI is technically capable of acting.
questions.risk: Unchecked autonomy can turn model capability into unauthorized real-world action.
questions.completionCondition: A trusted runtime independently verifies protected-action authorization and denies execution when valid human proof is absent.
nonClaims: Genesis does not yet claim cryptographically enforced L5 Human Sovereignty at runtime.

questions.question: Can Genesis give itself more power?
questions.plainLanguageAnswer: Genesis is governed by a no-self-escalation rule: it cannot legitimately grant itself permissions, credentials, roles, policy exceptions or trusted-device status.
questions.currentTruth: The rule is encoded in Owner Law, agent instructions and machine-readable governance. Runtime enforcement across every future tool boundary remains to be proven.
questions.peopleImpact: AI authority should not expand just because the AI requests it.
questions.risk: Self-escalation can bypass human intent and least-privilege boundaries.
questions.completionCondition: Every operational tool and delegated-agent path enforces non-amplifying authority and has negative tests for self-escalation.
nonClaims: Policy text alone is not proof that every future integration is enforcement-safe.

questions.question: Can Genesis perform a high-risk action without me knowing or approving it?
questions.plainLanguageAnswer: The intended answer is no. L5 actions are designed to require a fresh, action-bound human authorization before execution.
questions.currentTruth: Authorization request and receipt contracts exist, but the trusted WebAuthn and device-bound verifier is not implemented.
questions.peopleImpact: People should see and approve consequential actions before they happen.
questions.risk: Broad or reusable consent can be transformed into authority for a different or more dangerous action.
questions.completionCondition: WebAuthn user verification plus a recognized device-bound approval key is verified against the exact action digest, nonce and expiry before L5 execution.
nonClaims: A chat message, checkbox, JSON field or AI statement is not valid L5 approval.

questions.question: Can I stop Genesis or revoke its authority?
questions.plainLanguageAnswer: Genesis is designed so a human can revoke delegated authority and protected operations fail closed when required authorization is unavailable.
questions.currentTruth: Revocation is constitutional law and part of the authorization design; a complete runtime revocation service is not yet evidenced.
questions.peopleImpact: Consent that cannot be withdrawn is not meaningful control.
questions.risk: Persistent credentials or standing authority can outlive the person's intent.
questions.completionCondition: Revocation, expiry, verifier-unavailable and emergency-stop tests all prove protected actions are denied after authority is withdrawn.
nonClaims: Runtime revocation is not yet Verified.

questions.question: How do I know Genesis is not exaggerating what it can do?
questions.plainLanguageAnswer: Genesis uses explicit maturity labels and requires claims to follow evidence. Planned, simulated and unavailable capabilities must not be presented as verified.
questions.currentTruth: The capability register, claim-surface regression guard and CI checks exist and are exercised in the current stabilization stack.
questions.peopleImpact: A non-technical person should be able to tell the difference between a working capability, a prototype and a future goal.
questions.risk: Unsupported security claims create false confidence and can cause unsafe decisions.
questions.completionCondition: Every public operational claim maps to current reproducible evidence and CI rejects unsupported maturity promotion.
nonClaims: Passing claim-surface checks is not a certification of the whole platform.

questions.question: How can I know what Genesis actually did?
questions.plainLanguageAnswer: Consequential operations should produce attributable audit evidence. Current backend runtime roles can append to the canonical audit ledger but cannot update or delete it.
questions.currentTruth: Database migrations and CI privilege probes test append-only runtime-role behavior. End-to-end signed agent authorization receipts remain a Target.
questions.peopleImpact: People need a readable record of what acted, under whose authority, on what resource and with what result.
questions.risk: Without durable audit evidence, failures and abuse can be denied or misattributed.
questions.completionCondition: Protected agent actions create verifiable, action-bound receipts and audit records whose integrity, access controls and retention are independently tested.
nonClaims: The current database control is not a claim of cryptographic non-repudiation or full tamper-evidence.

questions.question: How does Genesis know who a person, device or agent really is?
questions.plainLanguageAnswer: Identity must be established separately from authorization. Genesis has a canonical human Identity service and DeviceTrust service; dedicated cryptographic agent identity remains future work.
questions.currentTruth: Human authentication and DeviceTrust code exist. Agent identity and production WebAuthn enrollment are not yet Verified.
questions.peopleImpact: An action should never gain authority merely because a name or label says it came from a trusted person or agent.
questions.risk: Impersonation and confused identity can transfer authority to the wrong actor.
questions.completionCondition: Humans, trusted approval devices and operational agents have cryptographically verifiable identities with lifecycle, rotation and revocation tests.
nonClaims: Device trust posture is not identity and is not authorization.

questions.question: What personal information does Genesis use, where does it go, and can I control it?
questions.plainLanguageAnswer: Genesis is intended to make collection, purpose, destination, retention and external sharing visible and controllable rather than hidden in technical implementation.
questions.currentTruth: Security and privacy documentation exists, but a complete user-facing data inventory, consent ledger and provider-egress enforcement layer is not yet evidenced.
questions.peopleImpact: People should understand data use without reading source code or a long legal document.
questions.risk: Unclear data flows can expose sensitive information or make consent meaningless.
questions.completionCondition: Automated data-flow tests and a human-readable Trust Center disclose collection, purpose, destination, retention, deletion and model-provider use for each data class.
nonClaims: Genesis does not yet claim complete provider-egress enforcement or training-use guarantees for external AI providers.

questions.question: What happens if malicious instructions try to manipulate Genesis?
questions.plainLanguageAnswer: Untrusted content must never become authority. Prompt text, retrieved documents and tool output are data unless a trusted policy boundary explicitly grants an action.
questions.currentTruth: The constitutional separation between information and authority is established, but a comprehensive prompt-injection and tool-abuse test suite is not yet present.
questions.peopleImpact: A webpage, email or document should not be able to trick an agent into acting with the person's privileges.
questions.risk: Indirect prompt injection can turn untrusted content into unauthorized tool use or data disclosure.
questions.completionCondition: Adversarial tests prove untrusted instructions cannot alter authority, bypass approval, exfiltrate protected data or broaden tool scope.
nonClaims: Prompt-injection resistance is not yet Verified.

questions.question: How can Genesis help distinguish authentic digital content from manipulated or AI-generated content?
questions.plainLanguageAnswer: Genesis should prefer verifiable provenance over guessing whether content looks synthetic.
questions.currentTruth: No C2PA implementation is currently evidenced in Genesis.
questions.peopleImpact: People need provenance they can inspect rather than unreliable 'fake or real' guesses.
questions.risk: Synthetic media and missing provenance can enable impersonation, fraud and misinformation.
questions.completionCondition: Genesis can create, preserve and validate supported provenance credentials and clearly distinguish verified provenance from unknown provenance.
nonClaims: Genesis does not claim perfect AI-content detection or universal authenticity determination.

questions.question: What happens when the AI is wrong or confidently invents an answer?
questions.plainLanguageAnswer: Model output is not evidence by itself. Genesis should distinguish source evidence, inference, uncertainty and unverified model statements.
questions.currentTruth: Claims-follow-evidence is a governance rule and capability maturity is explicit. Systematic model-quality evaluation and calibrated uncertainty testing remain a Target.
questions.peopleImpact: People should be able to see when an answer is supported, uncertain or unverified.
questions.risk: Overreliance on fluent but incorrect output can create bad technical, financial, security or personal decisions.
questions.completionCondition: Defined evaluation sets measure factuality, grounding, abstention and source attribution for each model-dependent Genesis use case.
nonClaims: Genesis does not claim that any language model is incapable of hallucination.

questions.question: Who is accountable when Genesis makes or carries out a consequential decision?
questions.plainLanguageAnswer: Genesis is designed to preserve the chain from human principal to policy to agent to tool to outcome instead of treating 'the AI' as an anonymous decision-maker.
questions.currentTruth: Governance and audit architecture exist. Complete action-bound signed receipts and production policy decisions are not yet Verified.
questions.peopleImpact: A person affected by an action should be able to understand who authorized it and what rule permitted it.
questions.risk: Opaque delegation can hide responsibility and make remediation difficult.
questions.completionCondition: Every protected action can be traced through authenticated principal, policy decision, exact request, agent/tool identity, receipt and outcome.
nonClaims: A receipt schema is not proof that a cryptographically verified receipt was produced.

questions.question: How will Genesis detect and reduce harmful bias or unfair treatment?
questions.plainLanguageAnswer: Genesis should measure decisions against defined fairness and harm criteria for the specific population and use case rather than claim that an AI is simply 'unbiased'.
questions.currentTruth: No project-wide fairness evaluation suite is currently evidenced.
questions.peopleImpact: People affected by automated decisions need measurable safeguards and routes for correction.
questions.risk: Model or data bias can produce systematically harmful outcomes.
questions.completionCondition: Each consequential AI use case defines affected populations, fairness risks, measurable evaluation criteria, remediation thresholds and appeal/review paths.
nonClaims: Genesis does not claim to be bias-free.

questions.question: Can a non-technical person understand what Genesis is doing and why?
questions.plainLanguageAnswer: Genesis is intended to expose the important decision, authority, risk and evidence in plain language, with technical detail available as a deeper layer rather than a prerequisite.
questions.currentTruth: Plain-language documentation is being developed, but formal usability and accessibility validation has not yet been recorded.
questions.peopleImpact: Control is not meaningful if only an engineer can understand the choice.
questions.risk: Technical interfaces can turn nominal consent into uninformed consent.
questions.completionCondition: Representative non-technical usability testing shows people can correctly identify what will happen, who authorized it, what data is used and how to decline or revoke.
nonClaims: Documentation quality has not yet been independently usability-tested.

questions.question: Will Genesis be transparent about the resources AI consumes?
questions.plainLanguageAnswer: Genesis should use ordinary deterministic software when it is sufficient, use AI when it adds measurable value, and report meaningful compute or external-service use where practical.
questions.currentTruth: No project-wide compute, energy or AI-call accounting system is currently evidenced.
questions.peopleImpact: People and organizations should be able to understand cost and resource consequences instead of treating AI compute as invisible.
questions.risk: Unbounded agent loops can waste compute, money, energy and time.
questions.completionCondition: AI-dependent workflows have bounded budgets, loop limits and measurable usage reporting appropriate to the deployment.
nonClaims: Genesis does not yet claim measured energy efficiency.

questions.question: Who controls Genesis today?
questions.plainLanguageAnswer: Within the current GitHub repository and Genesis governance model, AcingTime420 is the recorded human project principal. Genesis and its agents are subordinate to that human authority.
questions.currentTruth: The repository is under AcingTime420 and Owner Law defines human project authority. Repository governance records do not by themselves adjudicate trademarks, copyright assignments, corporate ownership or other legal title.
questions.peopleImpact: People should know who has project authority and should not be told that an AI owns or governs itself.
questions.risk: Ambiguous ownership and authority can conceal who is responsible for policy and product decisions.
questions.completionCondition: Project governance, legal entity/IP records where applicable, release signing authority and operational principals are documented without conflating repository control with legal ownership.
nonClaims: This machine-readable governance record is not legal proof of intellectual-property ownership.
